  "text": "On Monday, a woman came into the bakery and asked for a honey cake. She wore a yellow raincoat, although the afternoon was warm.

“Auntie Laila?” Imani asked.

The woman smiled. “That depends. Did my map help?”

Sami fetched the notebook from its shelf. Laila turned to Imani’s drawing and touched one of the blue posts with her fingertip.

“My brother painted those,” she said. “He got more paint on himself than on the gate.”

Nabil leaned over the counter. “Was it blue first, or green?”

“Green,” Laila said. “Then blue. Then green again, where the beans rubbed it off.”

Imani’s grandfather laughed. Laila studied his face for a moment and said his name. He looked surprised, then pleased, as though she had handed back something he had misplaced.

They shared the last honey cake at the little table by the window. Laila told them about a bell that had hung outside the school. When the bell went missing, the children had taken turns making its sound. She demonstrated, and Sami tried it too. His version made everyone laugh.

Before she left, Laila opened the notebook to a blank page. She drew a crooked bell and wrote the name of another street beneath it.

“Is there something there?” Imani asked.

“There was,” Laila said. “Someone might remember where it went.”"
